ideas.name: Native MT4/MT5 Strategy Tester report and TradingView 'List of trades' import, plus MT5 modelling-quality red flags
ideas.what: Accept the files traders already have, without converting them to CSV first. That means the MT5 Strategy Tester report as HTML (UTF-16) or XLSX, the MT4 report as HTM/CSV, the MT5 account statement as HTML, and the TradingView Strategy Tester 'List of trades' CSV (two rows per trade: Entry/Exit, Trade #, Type, Signal, Date/Time, Price, Contracts, Profit, Cumulative Profit, Run-up, Drawdown). Rebuild the closed-trade ledger and a balance curve from these files, tagged MEASURED and noted as 'derived from the uploaded report'. Read the report header too: initial deposit, modelling mode ('Every tick based on real ticks' vs '1 minute OHLC' vs 'Open prices only'), history quality %, spread setting and test period. Feed that header into new red flags: LOW_HISTORY_QUALITY, COARSE_MODELLING_MODE, FIXED_OR_CURRENT_SPREAD, SHORT_TEST_PERIOD and BALANCE_ONLY_CURVE (floating drawdown not visible). Where it goes: new parsers in audit/schema.py (a report_formats.py sibling), detection by sniffing the file, fixtures under tests/, and one line per new flag in docs/AUDIT_SAAS.md.
ideas.who_pays_and_why: All four retail segments. EA buyers get a vendor's MT5 report and want a verdict in one upload. EA and signal sellers export MT5 reports by default. Prop candidates on TradingView export 'List of trades'. Today the product needs hand-built CSVs, which is the biggest point where users drop off before paying. Every direct competitor takes MT reports natively.
ideas.evidence: QuantAnalyzer imports MT4 reports (htm/html/csv), MT5 reports and statements (htm/html), TradeStation (xml/mht/xlsx/csv), MultiCharts (xls/xlsx) and NinjaTrader (csv) (strategyquant.com/doc/quantanalyzer/formats-supported-in-quantanalyzer). EA X-Ray: 'upload your MT5 Strategy Tester report and get an instant evidence score and red flags: missing data years, martingale settings, fantasy fills, regime luck' (eaxray.com). ErgodicLabs does Monte Carlo on MT4/MT5/cTrader reports in the browser (ergodiclabs.co/monte-carlo). EA Auditor (MQL5 Market) loads an EA's backtest HTML report. MT5 exports only XLSX or HTML, not CSV (myforex.com mt5guide; proea.app). TradingView's List of Trades export has the columns above and needs a paid plan (tradingview.com support 43000613680; mylinedchart.com).
ideas.risk_or_rule_conflict: Low. Parsing only, with no broker connectivity. The file must stay the source: a curve rebuilt from closed trades must say that open (floating) drawdown is NOT_MEASURED. The header fields read from the report are MEASURED from the file but were set by the uploader, so the report should say 'as stated in the uploaded report'. Each new red flag needs a test and a line in the docs (Phase 16 rule). XLSX needs openpyxl, which should go in the 'web' extra, not in the core.

ideas.name: Trade statistics pack (profit factor, expectancy, payoff, win rate, max consecutive losses, SQN, concentration)
ideas.what: When trades are supplied, add a MEASURED trade-statistics section with: gross profit and loss, profit factor, expectancy per trade (currency and % of notional, and in R if a stop column exists), payoff ratio (average win / average loss), win rate, max consecutive wins and losses, Van Tharp SQN (sqrt(N)·mean/std of per-trade P&L, capped at N=100 by convention), average holding time for winners vs losers, long/short split, largest single trade as % of net, and the share of net P&L from the top 5 and top 10% of trades. Also add a PROFIT_CONCENTRATION red flag, for example when the top 5% of trades make up more than 50% of net P&L. Compute each statistic at 1x/2x/3x cost using the existing costs.py re-costing. Code goes in audit/engine.py (a new _trade_stats) and report.py.
ideas.who_pays_and_why: Everyone. These are the table-stakes numbers traders look at first. Without them the report reads as 'academic' next to a free MT5 report or Myfxbook, which makes the $49 hard to justify. They are also inputs for the Monte Carlo, prop-firm and martingale features.
ideas.evidence: TradingView's Performance Summary shows net profit, profit factor, max drawdown, win rate, Sharpe and Sortino, run-up, and long/short columns (tradingview.com/support/solutions/43000681683). EA Auditor scores 'profit factor, drawdown, win rate, trade count, risk, durability, expectancy'. Forex Factory threads quote 'SQN over 10, max DD 5%, PF 2.50, passes 1000 Monte Carlo rounds' when selling EAs (forexfactory.com/thread/1090747). Myfxbook's Advanced Statistics show expectancy and a risk-of-ruin table (blog.myfxbook.com/2010/12/13/risk-of-ruin). FX Blue shows winners vs losers, longs vs shorts, and MAE/MFE vs outcome (api.fxblue.com/faq/risk-statistics). overfit-detector includes 'profit concentration' as a fragility test (github.com/CyberTraderX/overfit-detector).
ideas.risk_or_rule_conflict: Low. Show raw values only. Do not repeat the 'SQN > 7 = holy grail' labels from Van Tharp marketing, and never write 'profitable system' (the English guard bans 'profitable'). Label profit factor at 1x cost as 'under the reference cost assumption' (DECLARED cost). The new red flag needs a test and a doc line.

ideas.name: Monte Carlo drawdown, risk of ruin and time under water from the trade sequence
ideas.what: Resample the supplied closed trades in three ways: reshuffle (order only, without replacement), resample with replacement, and block resample to keep streaks, with 1k–10k runs and a fixed seed. Report the distribution of max drawdown (p50/p95/p99), longest time under water, max consecutive losses, and final P&L percentiles. Add a risk-of-ruin table: the share of resampled paths that touch −10/−20/−30/−50% of the declared starting capital, using the sizing as supplied. Keep everything as quantile tables plus a fan chart, and state the exchangeability assumption. Reuse research/bootstrap.py for the stationary variant. Code goes in the audit engine as a new 'resampling' section with its own seed recorded, so the output stays byte-reproducible.
ideas.who_pays_and_why: EA and signal sellers want a 'passes Monte Carlo' line for their marketing. Buyers and prop candidates want to know how bad a drawdown the same trades could plausibly give. Forum users name this as the most valued robustness test, and every competitor that charges money leads with it.
ideas.evidence: QuantAnalyzer: 'two separate Monte Carlo tests with 9+ simulation types' (strategyquant.com/quantanalyzer/monte-carlo). SQX 'Monte Carlo trades manipulation – reshuffled, some omitted' (strategyquant.com/doc/strategyquant/monte-carlo-trades-manipulation). Build Alpha lists Monte Carlo among 12+ robustness tests ($447/quarter). EA Verdict's $19 audit includes 'Monte-Carlo stress testing with equity fan charts, max-drawdown percentiles, streaks, time under water, ruin probability at seven sizings' (eaverdict.com/audits/quantum-titan). ErgodicLabs Solo/Pro sells 10k/50k-iteration Monte Carlo (ergodiclabs.co). Myfxbook's risk-of-ruin table shows the probability of losing 10–100% (blog.myfxbook.com). FX Blue uses a Cox & Miller risk of ruin (api.fxblue.com/faq/risk-statistics). Forex Factory: 'Monte Carlo shuffles the order of trades thousands of times… worst-case drawdown and probability of reaching profit targets' (forexfactory.com/thread/post/15267110).
ideas.risk_or_rule_conflict: Medium, over wording. v9's UNSUPPORTABLE_CONTEXTS already lists 'monte_carlo', so any final-P&L percentile must never be phrased as expected or likely profit. Title the section 'Resampled history of the supplied trades (not a forecast)'. Lead with drawdown and ruin, not gains. State that resampling inherits any fabrication or selection in the file, and that iid resampling breaks serial dependence. Record the seed and method in the JSON thresholds.

ideas.name: Martingale / grid / averaging-down / no-stop detection red flags
ideas.what: New trade-level red flags. MARTINGALE_SIZING: position size after a loss is systematically larger than after a win (a size ratio conditional on the previous outcome, with a sign/permutation test). GRID_AVERAGING: overlapping same-direction positions opened at worse prices while earlier ones are still open. MANY_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS. NEGATIVE_PAYOFF_HIGH_WINRATE: win rate > 85% with average loss several times the average win. NO_STOP_EVIDENCE: max adverse trade far beyond the typical loss. HIDDEN_FLOATING_DRAWDOWN: balance-only curve plus overlapping positions. All are computed from quantity and timestamps already in the trades schema. Code goes in audit/redflags.py, with synthetic fixtures (a martingale sequence, a grid sequence and a clean one) in tests.
ideas.who_pays_and_why: EA buyers first. Martingale or grid disguised as 'smart recovery' is their top fear, and a $19–29 pre-purchase check pays for itself against a $300–1,000 EA or a lost account. Honest sellers pay to show 'no martingale pattern detected in the supplied trades'. Prop firms (B2B) screen for martingale, which most firms ban.
ideas.evidence: MQL5 blogs 'Your EA's Smart Recovery Is Martingale in Disguise (How to Check)' (mql5.com/en/blogs/post/768904) and 'How to Choose a Safe EA (Avoid Grid, Martingale & Over-Optimization)' (mql5.com/en/blogs/post/766446): 'sellers often avoid showing the equity line because it shows the usage of Grid/Martingale'. EA X-Ray flags 'martingale settings' (eaxray.com). ErgodicLabs advertises 'martingale detection' (ergodiclabs.co/monte-carlo). EA Verdict includes 'Martingale/grid/hedging forensics' in its $19 audit. Prop firms detect 'consistent doubling of lot sizes after losses (Martingale)' (fxnx.com prop-firm EA rules; tradingviewcopier.com). MQL5 forum threads on scam EAs (mql5.com/en/forum/457568).
ideas.risk_or_rule_conflict: Medium, over wording and fairness. Describe a statistical pattern ('position size increases after losses, consistent with martingale-style scaling'), never accuse the vendor of fraud. With a third party's report, add 'the vendor was not consulted'. Each flag needs a test and a doc line, and FAIL vs WARN severity must be justified in the docs. Pyramiding by design can false-positive, so state that limitation.

ideas.name: Public verification page and embeddable badge (opt-in, audit ID, dated, revocable)
ideas.what: The owner can publish a paid audit to /v/{public_id}. The page shows: class A–D, the six dimension statuses, audit date, engine version, dataset digest, declared trials, OOS start and cost, and the full limitations block. Add an SVG badge (/v/{public_id}/badge.svg) plus HTML/BBCode/Markdown embed snippets for forum signatures, Telegram, websites and README files. The badge shows only the class, the ID, the date and the words 'Statistical audit of supplied data – not verified with a broker – not a performance guarantee' / 'Auditoría estadística de datos aportados – no verificados con el bróker – no garantiza resultados'. Never show growth, return or profit on the badge. Also: expiry (for example 90 days, then 'expired' is rendered), a revoke button, a list of other published audits of the same dataset digest, and a public count of versions audited by that account for the same strategy name, so selectively published badges are visible. Code: store.py gets a published flag, public_id, expires_at and revoked_at. web.py gets public GET routes with no token and the SVG template. The guard runs on the badge and page text.
ideas.who_pays_and_why: EA sellers, signal sellers and course/academy owners. It is the only feature that turns the audit into a marketing asset they display, and that justifies a premium 'seller certificate' tier of about $99–149. It is also the main source of virality: every embed links back, which is how Myfxbook widgets spread as forum signatures.
ideas.evidence: AntiOverfit: 'Check an EA' €97 includes 'no badge, public certificate or public Audit ID'. Higher tiers let developers 'request a private audit first, with a public certificate only if the result is suitable and approved'. Public IDs look like AOA-2026-0009 (antioverfit.com/services, antioverfit.com/contact). Myfxbook widgets are 'a way of advertising your trading system… forum post/signature (BB code)', and only fully verified accounts show 'Verified by Myfxbook.com' (myfxbook.com/widgets; myfxbook forum 987357). Fewer than 5% of MQL5 Market EAs link to a verified live signal (blodsalgo.com MQL5 market guide), so buyers have an unmet need for proof. The MinervaScore paper ties a 0–100 score to a binary 'Robustness Seal' (arxiv.org/abs/2608.23808).
ideas.risk_or_rule_conflict: HIGH, the main rule conflict. (1) A badge can be read as a performance guarantee or as broker-verified like Myfxbook. Never use 'verified', 'certified profitable' or 'verificado' on it. The wording must say it is a statistical audit of supplied data only, not broker-reconciled, not a forecast. Extend the guard with patterns such as 'verified track record', 'certified', 'aprobado', 'pasarás' and 'certificado de rentabilidad', and test them in en and es. (2) Selection bias: sellers will publish only class A. Show the version count and trials on the public page, and allow publishing any class. (3) MQL5 Market rules forbid 'links or images of awards, certificates or testimonials… from third-party companies' in product listings (mql5.com/en/market/rules). The badge's reach is therefore the seller's own site, Telegram, Forex Factory and YouTube, and the ToS must say that. (4) The CNMV's 2026 finfluencer guide requires promotional content on high-risk products to be 'true, fair, clear and not misleading' (cnmv.es GuiaparaFinfluencers.pdf). The ToS must forbid using the badge in claims of returns, and let us revoke it. (5) Only an owner can publish a page. Never publish an audit of a third party's file. (6) Public pages must not expose the client description, uploads or tokens (no secrets in artifacts).

ideas.name: Prop-firm rule replay and resampled pass/breach rates (evidence-deflated)
ideas.what: Versioned, dated rule presets as data files: target %, max loss static / trailing EOD / trailing intraday, daily loss anchor, min trading days, consistency or best-day rule. Presets are 'modelled on publicly posted rules of <firm type> as of <date>', and users can set custom values. Two outputs. (a) Historical replay: walk the actual supplied trade sequence and list every date a rule would have been breached or the target met. (b) Resampled rates: the share of block-bootstrapped sequences that hit the target before a breach, and the share that breach first, with 95% CIs, plus expected attempts and fee spend at a user-entered challenge fee. The differentiator is an 'evidence-deflated' row that reruns the resampling with per-trade expectancy shrunk to the lower bootstrap/DSR-consistent band, so an overfit backtest does not show a flattering rate. Also report the prop 'consistency' metric (best day / total). Needs intraday timestamps for the daily rules. Intraday trailing needs MAE, which is NOT_MEASURED unless the TradingView Run-up/Drawdown columns are present.
ideas.who_pays_and_why: Prop-challenge candidates, a large Spanish-speaking segment. Fees run from €79 to €1,080 per attempt ($540 for 100k), and industry estimates put combined pass rates near 10%, so a $29–49 check before paying a fee is easy to justify. Prop firms and academies (B2B) could use it to pre-screen or coach.
ideas.evidence: Pass-probability calculators are everywhere and free: TradeZella (1,000 runs), Tanto (10,000 runs with FTMO/Apex/Topstep presets), Prop Firm Pal, TradeSearcher, PropFirms Codes, TradeLens, Funded.Now (search results for 'prop firm challenge pass probability calculator'). LuxAlgo open-sourced prop-firm-sim (MIT, 66 stars) with block-bootstrapped R-multiples, static/EOD/intraday trailing rules, daily-loss anchors, consistency rules, expected attempts, cost and 'optimal risk sizing' (github.com/LuxAlgo/prop-firm-sim). 'The intraday variant… routinely cuts pass probability by a third versus the static rule' (luxalgo.com search snippet). FTMO fees are €79–€1,080, and estimates put stage-1 pass near 35% and combined near 10% (arxum.com prop-trading-statistics; traderssecondbrain.com prop-firm-pass-rate). Topstep and FTMO consistency / best-day rules are 50% (tradedupe.com; newyorkcityservers.com). EA Verdict includes 'prop-firm rule replay (FTMO, generic profiles)' in a $19 audit. Backtrex (from €29/month) simulates trailing DD and consistency rules.
ideas.risk_or_rule_conflict: HIGH. A 'pass probability' is a probability of hitting a profit target, so it reads close to 'you will make money'. Name it 'share of resampled sequences of the supplied trades that met the rule's target before a limit (not a prediction)'. Always show the breach rate first and the evidence-deflated row next to the raw one. Never write 'you will pass' or 'pasarás', and add those to the guard. Never recommend a sizing or firm: LuxAlgo's 'optimal risk sizing' would break the 'never recommends' rule, so show a table across sizings without picking one. Using firm names implies affiliation and goes stale, so use dated generic presets, no affiliate links, and a 'verify rules with the firm' note. The free calculators mean this is a differentiator inside the audit, not a standalone paid product.

ideas.name: Tiered pricing: free instant score, cheap buyer check, full audit, seller certificate, developer subscription
ideas.what: Replace the single $49 price with tiers, keeping the forced free mode when any Stripe variable is missing. (0) Free instant score: class, the dimension grid and red-flag names, watermarked, no numbers behind the flags. This is the lead magnet. (1) 'EA buyer check' at about $19–29: red flags, trade stats, Monte Carlo drawdown, and a 'questions to ask the vendor' list, private only. (2) Full audit at about $49–79: everything, including prop replay and version compare. (3) 'Seller certificate' at about $99–149: full audit, public page and badge valid 90 days, and one re-audit. (4) Developer subscription at about $19–29/month: unlimited re-audits, version comparison, trials ledger, and backtest-vs-live drift checks. (5) B2B later at about $199–499/month. Implementation: one STRIPE_PRICE_ID_<TIER> environment variable per tier (no defaults), an entitlement column in store.py, report sections gated by tier, and webhook tests with the existing HMAC helper.
ideas.who_pays_and_why: This matches willingness to pay to the segment. EA buyers pay once and little (competitors charge $19–€29). Sellers pay more for a public asset (AntiOverfit €97–€390). Active developers and prop candidates pay monthly, which trading-journal subscriptions already show they accept.
ideas.evidence: EA Verdict $19 per audit. EA X-Ray: free instant score, €29 human-verified audit (eaxray.com). AntiOverfit €97 / €390 / from €790 (antioverfit.com/services). ErgodicLabs: free browser app, Professional $497 one-time (ergodiclabs.co). QuantAnalyzer Pro ~$349 plus $300/year for updates, and its free version is capped (Compare limited to the first 50 trades, portfolio to 4 strategies). TradeZella $35/$59/$99 per month, Edgewonk $197/year, Tradervue $29.95–49.95/month, Darwinex Zero €38/month, Backtrex from €29/month.
ideas.risk_or_rule_conflict: Low to medium. Keep 'no secret has a default' and free mode forced when any Stripe variable is missing. Every tier's pages must pass the en/es guard. Do not market the certificate tier as 'get verified'. Price anchoring must not imply that a higher tier gets a better class: the verdict must be identical across tiers, and only the sections shown and the public page differ. Say this explicitly in the docs and test it.

ideas.name: Charts in the self-contained HTML report (inline SVG)
ideas.what: Add server-rendered inline SVG, with no JavaScript and no CDN, so the report stays self-contained and byte-reproducible. Charts: equity and underwater drawdown; the equity curve at 1x/2x/3x cost; rolling Sharpe with the OOS start marked; a monthly returns heatmap; the per-trade P&L distribution; the Monte Carlo drawdown fan; the bootstrap Sharpe band; and, when variants are labelled, a parameter heatmap. Code goes in report.py as small SVG helpers, each with a unit test on the number of points and the axes.
ideas.who_pays_and_why: Every segment. Without charts the report looks weaker than a free QuantStats tear sheet or MT5 report, and screenshots of charts are what people share on Telegram and Forex Factory. The equity line also exposes grid or martingale behaviour that sellers hide.
ideas.evidence: QuantStats HTML tear sheets include returns plots, drawdown charts, rolling metrics, distribution histograms and monthly heatmaps (github.com/ranaroussi/quantstats). SQX's Walk-Forward Matrix sells a 3D view of results (strategyquant.com/doc/strategyquant/walk-forward-matrix). The overfit-detector HTML embeds equity, Monte Carlo and parameter-surface charts. The MQL5 blog notes 'sellers often avoid showing the equity line because it shows Grid/Martingale' (mql5.com/en/blogs/post/766446). ErgodicLabs offers a free 'Backtest Graph Builder' (ergodiclabs.co/chart-rebuilder).
ideas.risk_or_rule_conflict: Low. Label the Monte Carlo fan as resampled history, not a projection cone. Never draw extrapolated future equity. Chart titles and axis labels must pass the guard. Watermark preview charts.

ideas.name: Version comparison with an automatic trials ledger
ideas.what: Compare two or more audits side by side: deltas in PSR, DSR, bootstrap bands, OOS gap, cost break-even, trade stats, Monte Carlo p95 drawdown and red flags. Each new version of the same strategy name from the same account adds to a trials ledger, which is shown next to the client's declared trials and used as a floor for the DSR sensitivity row ('you have audited 7 versions of this strategy with us'). Code: store.py (a strategy_key and audit lineage), a /compare route, and report sections.
ideas.who_pays_and_why: Developers iterating on EAs and Pine scripts. This is the reason to subscribe rather than buy once. Academies can use it to show students' progress. It also sets the product apart on honesty: the tool itself tracks the p-hacking.
ideas.evidence: QuantAnalyzer paywalls compare: the free version limits 'Compare results to the first 50 trades only' (QuantAnalyzer pricing search result). ErgodicLabs Pro adds 'multi-strategy Compare' and 'multi-EA Portfolio Mode' (ergodiclabs.co). The MinervaScore paper notes that standard summaries 'do not record how many candidates were tried' (arxiv.org/abs/2608.23808).
ideas.risk_or_rule_conflict: Low. The ledger count comes from our own records, so tag it MEASURED 'within this service', while the client's trials stay DECLARED. Privacy: lineage uses the account's own audits only. Retention purge must keep the ledger count (the id, digest and class are already kept).

ideas.name: Backtest-vs-live reconciliation and drift check (uploaded statements only)
ideas.what: The client uploads the backtest trades plus a live or demo account statement (MT5 statement HTML, TradingView export, or a CSV journal) for the same strategy. Report: matched vs missing trades, per-trade slippage and cost difference, live Sharpe and drawdown against the backtest's bootstrap bands ('live results fall inside or outside the range the backtest's own resampling produced'), and a CUSUM-style drift statistic over time. This can be sold as a monthly re-check.
ideas.who_pays_and_why: Buyers checking whether an EA they bought matches its advertised backtest. Sellers wanting to show that their live signal is consistent with the backtest. Developers monitoring decay. It creates recurring revenue in the subscription tier.
ideas.evidence: EA Auditor 'audits backtest reports, reviews posted developer signals, and cross-verifies the two' (MQL5 Market product 165487). AlgoChef's 'Health Score tracks your strategy against statistical expectations… when performance drifts beyond normal bounds, you get alerted' (algochef.app). MQL5 forum threads complain that EAs 'show good backtesting results but always fail when used in live environments' (mql5.com/en/forum/337020). Collective2 re-marks prices to broker executions with an audit log (support.collective2.com).
ideas.risk_or_rule_conflict: Medium. There is no broker connectivity: statements are uploaded files, so the report must say 'as supplied, not reconciled with the broker' and must not imply Myfxbook-style verification. Never say 'live results confirm profits'. Phrase it as consistency with the backtest's distribution. Any drift alert must not become a trading instruction (no 'stop/start trading' recommendations).

ideas.name: Parameter-stability / plateau analysis from a labelled variants matrix
ideas.what: Allow variant column headers such as 'fast=10;slow=50', plus a declared 'selected' column. Compute: the rank of the selected variant; the median Sharpe of its grid neighbours divided by its own Sharpe (plateau ratio); the share of variants with positive Sharpe; an ISOLATED_PEAK red flag; and a 1-D/2-D heatmap. This complements the existing CSCV PBO. Code goes in schema.parse_variants_csv (header parsing) and an engine _plateau.
ideas.who_pays_and_why: More advanced developers (StrategyQuant, Build Alpha, Python users) who already run grid searches. It targets the 'you optimised on a spike' failure that PBO alone explains poorly to retail users. It adds depth to the full and certificate tiers.
ideas.evidence: SQX sells 'System Parameter Permutation (SPP) and Optimization profile' and the WF Matrix to 'spot local maximums… clustered areas' (strategyquant.com robustness docs). Build Alpha lists 'Parameter Permutations' among its 12+ tests (buildalpha.com). overfit-detector includes 'parameter-plateau analysis'. Pardo and the LuxAlgo library: 'if length 20 backtests well, 17–24 should backtest comparably: the setting sits on a plateau' (luxalgo.com/library/concept/parameter-stability). Spanish sources name 'fragilidad paramétrica' as a key overfitting sign (tradingwyckoff.com validar-estrategia).
ideas.risk_or_rule_conflict: Low. The grid and the selected variant are DECLARED, and the client could upload a curated neighbourhood, so say so. The new red flag needs a test and a doc line. Do not suggest 'better' parameters, since that would be a recommendation.

ideas.name: Walk-forward results evaluation (WFE and OOS-window consistency)
ideas.what: Accept an optional walk-forward table (window, IS start/end, OOS start/end, IS metric, OOS metric) or per-window OOS equity. Report: walk-forward efficiency (OOS/IS annualised, following Pardo), the share of OOS windows with positive Sharpe, and the dispersion of OOS results. When OOS equity is uploaded, run PSR and DSR on the stitched OOS segment only. Otherwise, fall back to the existing rolling windows to report k-split consistency of the single curve.
ideas.who_pays_and_why: StrategyQuant, Build Alpha and EA Studio users, many from the Spanish SQX academies, who already produce walk-forward output and want an independent read of it. It fills the gap left by having only one declared OOS split today.
ideas.evidence: SQX's Walk-Forward Matrix is a headline feature of the $1,490+ tiers (strategyquant.com/doc/strategyquant/walk-forward-matrix; algotrading.space pricing). Build Alpha includes Walk-Forward. Pardo defines WFE, with >0.5 used as a robustness threshold (mql5.com/en/articles/23250; luxalgo walk-forward concept). Spanish SQX courses: Quantified Models máster €1,999–2,499, Angel Talavera, SQX Academy (quantifiedmodels.com; angeltalavera.com; sqx.academy).
ideas.risk_or_rule_conflict: Low to medium. The re-optimisation process is DECLARED; only uploaded OOS equity is MEASURED. The audit must not re-run optimisation (it executes nothing). Any new threshold such as WFE ≥ 0.5 needs a test and a doc line, and changes to the verdict dimensions need docs.

ideas.name: Sizing what-if table (no 'optimal')
ideas.what: Using the Monte Carlo engine, show max-drawdown p95 and ruin shares at several fixed-fractional risk levels (for example 0.25/0.5/1/2% per trade) or lot multipliers, as a neutral table.
ideas.who_pays_and_why: Prop candidates and EA buyers who ask 'how big can I size this without blowing the account'. It is standard in paid tools.
ideas.evidence: EA Verdict: 'ruin probability calculations at seven different sizings' ($19). QuantAnalyzer: 'Money management, What-If' simulations (strategyquant.com/quantanalyzer). LuxAlgo prop-firm-sim outputs 'optimal risk sizing'.
ideas.risk_or_rule_conflict: Medium. Choosing an 'optimal' or 'recommended' size would break 'never recommends', so show a table only with no highlighted row. Present drawdown and ruin, not projected gains.

ideas.name: Trader-behaviour attributes (Darwinex-style, generic)
ideas.what: Trade-derived behaviour scores: loss aversion or disposition effect (holding losers longer than winners), duration consistency, exit asymmetry (MFE/MAE use when Run-up/Drawdown columns exist), long/short skill split, and time-of-day or weekday concentration. Present raw measures with plain-language definitions, not a proprietary 0–10 score.
ideas.who_pays_and_why: Discretionary and prop traders, who are less served by the overfitting statistics. Darwinex is Madrid-based and well known in the Spanish-speaking community, so these concepts will be familiar. It adds depth to the subscription tier.
ideas.evidence: Darwinex's 12 investable attributes include Loss Aversion, R+/R− consistency, Duration Consistency, Open/Close Strategy and Capacity (help.darwinex.com/what-are-investable-attributes). Darwinex Zero charges €38/month to build a rated track record (blog.darwinex.com darwinex-zero). FX Blue shows MAE/MFE vs outcome (api.fxblue.com/faq/risk-statistics).
ideas.risk_or_rule_conflict: Low. Do not use the 'D-Score' or 'DARWIN' names (trademarks), and do not imply investability or eligibility for investor capital. Label MAE-dependent measures NOT_MEASURED when the columns are missing.

ideas.name: Signed audit JSON (tamper-evident report)
ideas.what: Sign the canonical audit.json (and the badge/public-page payload) with an Ed25519 key taken from the environment, with no default. Publish the public key at /.well-known/audit-key and add a 'verify' CLI and route that checks both the signature and the digests. Unsigned in free mode, and labelled as such.
ideas.who_pays_and_why: Supports the seller-certificate tier and B2B: a third party (a buyer, prop firm or academy) can check that a PDF or JSON shown to them was not edited.
ideas.evidence: AuditZK 'produces a signed report that anyone can verify without requiring trust' (auditzk.com/track-record). AntiOverfit uses public audit IDs (antioverfit.com). The current product already publishes sha256 digests and byte-reproducibility (docs/AUDIT_SAAS.md).
ideas.risk_or_rule_conflict: Low. The key comes from the environment only and must never be logged. A signature proves the report is ours and unedited; it does not prove the uploaded data is genuine, and the verify page must say so.

ideas.name: B2B: organisation API, white-label, cohort view for academies and prop firms
ideas.what: Organisation accounts with hashed API keys for batch audits (JSON in, JSON out), a white-label header and logo on reports, and a cohort dashboard for an academy class or prop applicants. The dashboard is ranked by evidence (DSR, class, red flags), never by return. It also offers exportable 'student robustness report' certificates, using the same badge wording rules.
ideas.who_pays_and_why: Spanish-speaking academies that charge €2,000–3,500 per student and want an objective grading tool and a differentiator. Prop firms and evaluation platforms screening EA users for martingale or overfit behaviour. Higher contract value at about $199–499/month, but a longer sales cycle.
ideas.evidence: Quantified Models máster costs €1,999–2,499 (quantifiedmodels.com; toulh.com). StatOasis Algo Trading Masterclass costs $3,499 (statoasis.com/products). Other Spanish academies include Academia Trading Algorítmico, Easy Trading Academy, Quant Vision Academy and SQX Academy. Prop firms detect martingale and toxic flow from trade patterns (fxnx.com; quantvps.com). Tradecopia charges $49.99–149.99/month for risk tooling (tradecopia.com).
ideas.risk_or_rule_conflict: Medium. API keys are our own service credentials, not broker keys: hash them, no defaults, and keep them out of reports. Ingestion stays upload-only, with no pulling from broker APIs. Cohort rankings must not become performance leaderboards or marketing of returns (guard plus CNMV fairness). Any screening use by prop firms must be described as statistical analysis, not a hiring or credit decision. Data processing agreements and retention (purge --yes) are needed for clients' users.

ideas.name: 'Questions to ask the vendor' checklist for EA buyers
ideas.what: Text generated from which fields are NOT_MEASURED or flagged. Examples: 'Ask for the modelling mode and history quality', 'Ask how many parameter sets were tried', 'Ask for a live signal of at least N months (the minimum track record length from the PSR is N)', 'Ask for the equity (floating) curve, not only the balance'. Bilingual, and added to the buyer tier.
ideas.who_pays_and_why: EA buyers, the largest and least technical segment. It turns the statistics into something they can act on, and it is shareable content that drives SEO and virality in forums.
ideas.evidence: MQL5 blog 'How to Verify an EA Is Real (Before You Lose $500): Myfxbook, Audited Accounts, Forward Testing' (mql5.com/en/blogs/post/769042). 'How to audit any EA backtest in 10 minutes (before you pay a cent)' (mql5.com/en/blogs/post/774579). ErgodicLabs '5 Red Flags Hiding in the Backtest Report' (ergodiclabs.co). EarnForex and Forex Factory 'Tips To Avoid Scammers At The MQL5 Market' threads.
ideas.risk_or_rule_conflict: Low. Keep the tone neutral and non-accusatory. The checklist must not say 'buy' or 'don't buy' (no recommendations). Guard in en and es.

pricing_benchmarks: Current product: USD 49 flat per audit (AUDIT_PRICE_USD_CENTS=4900 in docs/AUDIT_SAAS.md).
EA Verdict: USD 19 per independent EA audit (HTML). Six-dimension verdict, Monte Carlo fan, ruin at 7 sizings, prop-rule replay, martingale forensics (eaverdict.com/audits/quantum-titan).
EA X-Ray: free instant 0–100 evidence score from an MT5 report; EUR 29 human-verified audit (eaxray.com).

AntiOverfit: 'Check an EA' EUR 97 (private score, no badge, no public certificate or Audit ID); private robustness audit EUR 390; robustness improvement from EUR 790; public certificate with an Audit ID only if the result is suitable and approved (antioverfit.com/services, /contact).
ErgodicLabs Edge Matrix: free in-browser app; Solo/Pro tiers; Professional USD 497 one-time with lifetime updates (ergodiclabs.co).

QuantAnalyzer Pro: about USD 349 license plus USD 300/year for updates. The free tier caps money management and equity control at 30% of trades, portfolio at 4 strategies, and compare at the first 50 trades (strategyquant.com/quantanalyzer/pricing via search).
StrategyQuant X: Starter USD 1,290, Professional USD 1,490, Ultimate USD 2,900 one-time, or 12 instalments of 129/149/290 (algotrading.space; newyorkcityservers.com).
Build Alpha: USD 447/quarter, USD 997/year, USD 1,997 lifetime (the page title shows USD 1,497) (buildalpha.com/licensing).
TradeZella: USD 35 / 59 / 99 per month (26 / 44 / 74 billed annually) since July 2026 (tradezella.com/blog/tradezella-pricing).
Edgewonk: USD 197/year. Tradervue: USD 29.95–49.95/month (edgewonk.com/pricing; supertrader.me comparison).
TradeTanto: journal USD 14.99–39.99/month; its prop-firm Monte Carlo simulator is free (tradetanto.com).

Prop-firm pass-probability calculators are free: TradeZella, Tanto, Prop Firm Pal, TradeSearcher, PropFirms Codes, TradeLens, Funded.Now. LuxAlgo prop-firm-sim is open source under MIT (github.com/LuxAlgo/prop-firm-sim).
Backtrex: free (5 backtests/day), paid from EUR 29/month, with prop-rule simulation (backtrex.com).
Darwinex Zero: EUR 38/month to build a risk-rated track record on virtual capital (blog.darwinex.com; propfirm201.com).
Myfxbook: free. Fully verified accounts may sell premium access for USD 20–100/month (myfxbook.com/help premium-account-access).
Collective2: leaders charge USD 25–300/month; USD 30 track-record reset (trade.collective2.com; collective2 FAQ).

FTMO challenge fee: EUR 79 (10k, 1-step) to EUR 1,080 (200k, 2-step); USD 540 for 100k. Industry estimates put stage-1 pass near 35% and combined near 10% (luxalgo.com/prop-firms/ftmo; arxum.com; traderssecondbrain.com).

Spanish-language algo education: Quantified Models StrategyQuant máster EUR 1,999 early / EUR 2,499 (quantifiedmodels.com; toulh.com). StatOasis Algo Trading Masterclass USD 3,499 (statoasis.com/products).
B2B-adjacent tooling: Tradecopia risk and copy tooling USD 49.99–149.99/month (tradecopia.com).
